articles.summary: Two technical white papers and a counter-drone Fly Away Kit response submitted to U.S. Army xTech as the Company evaluates NATO procurement opportunities DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- NUBURU, Inc. (NYSE American: BURU) (“NUBURU” or the “Company”) today announced that Tekne S.p.A. (“Tekne”), its 70%-owned electronic warfare and tactical vehicle subsidiary, has submitted two technical white papers to the U.S. Army’s Spectrum Enabled Warfare xTech competition and a response to the C-UAS Fly Away Kit xTech competition. NUBURU is also reviewing NATO procurement opportunities. The procurement initiatives follow NUBURU’s completion of the Tekne acquisition on October 15, 2026. Tekne designs and manufactures electronic warfare systems and specialty and tactical vehicles in Italy. In its October 22, 2026 commercial update announcing Gianluca Trezza’s appointment as Tekne CEO, NUBURU disclosed approximately $96.8 million in remaining order and program value. The same update identified approximately $259.8 million in additional gross pipeline across 41 prospective opportunities, including $181.5 million in military and defense applications. “Tekne gives our U.S. defense strategy an operating industrial base and an existing product portfolio,” said Alessandro Zamboni, Executive Chairman and Co-CEO of NUBURU. “These Army submissions are a concrete step in matching those capabilities to customer requirements. We are developing local partnerships to support technical evaluations and future commercial opportunities.” Three procurement initiatives U.S. Army – Spectrum Enabled Warfare. Tekne submitted two technical white papers covering passive sensing and tactical surveillance, and electronic countermeasures. Under the published competition terms, up to 15 finalists may be invited to a live Army-led Soldier exercise in 2027. Up to five eventual winners may receive an additional $150,000 each and be considered for follow-on agreements. The competition provides up to $1.5 million in total cash prizes and a separate potential funding pool of up to $6 million for follow-on prototype agreements. U.S. Army – C-UAS Fly Away Kit. Tekne has submitted a response to this competition for portable, modular counter-drone systems for expeditionary sites, ahead of the November 17, 2026 deadline. The published terms provide up to $1 million in total cash prizes and a separate potential funding pool of up to $5 million for follow-on prototype agreements. These figures and the Spectrum figures above are competition-wide pools, not awards to Tekne. Follow-on agreements are subject to separate selection, available funding and applicable requirements. NATO – portable jamming kits. NUBURU is reviewing NATO Allied Command Transformation’s tender for six portable GNSS and drone-link jamming kits, due November 30, 2026, and monitoring future competitions for NATO’s Drone Edge counter-drone marketplace. What Tekne brings to U.S. and allied programs NUBURU Defense LLC is positioning Tekne’s Tactical Bubble and J4 electronic warfare systems and its tactical vehicles for U.S. and allied requirements for mobile counter-drone and electronic warfare capability. The Company plans to pursue direct bids and partner-led proposals against each program’s eligibility, qualification and support requirements. These transportable and vehicle-mounted systems are engineered and manufactured at Tekne’s Italian facilities. In 2027, Tekne plans to pursue demonstrations, technical evaluations and customer meetings in the United States. The Army’s publicly listed 2027 test range events provide a potential route for industry to test systems and interoperability in degraded operating conditions. NUBURU is assessing a Washington, D.C.–Northern Virginia presence to coordinate local partners, technical support and program requirements. Alongside Tekne, NUBURU plans to pursue U.S. commercial channels for Lyocon’s laser and photonics subsystems and Orbit’s operational resilience software for continuity planning, incident coordination and auditable reporting. The Company is also evaluating whether to broaden its previously announced collaboration with Maddox Defense Incorporated for the U.S. dual-use market, including defense, civil protection, emergency response and firefighting. The review considers how Tekne, Lyocon and Orbit capabilities could complement Maddox Defense’s U.S. commercial capabilities. NUBURU’s longer-term goal is to establish a U.S. hangar to house selected Defense & Security platform systems and support customer demonstrations and technical evaluations. The plan depends on site availability, funding and applicable approvals. “For each opportunity, we’re deciding which capabilities we can supply directly and where a partner would help us integrate and support the system,” said Dario Barisoni, Co-CEO of NUBURU and CEO of NUBURU Defense LLC. “Our aim is to progress from demonstrations and qualification to commercial deployments that we can support over the life of the system.” U.S. counter-drone procurement in 2026 Recent U.S. counter-drone procurements include a contract with a $500 million maximum ordering ceiling, a $464.8 million Army production award for high-energy laser systems, and an initial task order of approximately $87 million for tactical command-and-control software. These examples illustrate procurement activity across three distinct areas and provide market context for NUBURU’s U.S. strategy. About NUBURU, Inc. NUBURU, Inc. (NYSE American: BURU) develops software-orchestrated, hardware-enabled systems for defense and security, critical infrastructure and digital resilience. Its dual-use Defense & Security platform brings together directed-energy and other non-kinetic technologies, electronic warfare and defense mobility, operational resilience software, and advanced manufacturing and sustainment. NUBURU seeks to integrate these modular capabilities around customer requirements and support them over their operational life. For more information, visit www.nuburu.net and follow NUBURU on X . About NUBURU Defense LLC NUBURU Defense LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of NUBURU, Inc., supports industrial development, technology integration and commercialization for the Company’s Defense & Security platform. It holds a 70% controlling interest in Tekne S.p.A. and controls Orbit S.r.l. through board appointment rights . NUBURU Defense Italy S.r.l. supports the coordination and development of the Company’s Italian defense platform. Tekne develops electronic warfare systems and designs and manufactures specialty and tactical vehicles. Orbit provides operational resilience software for business continuity planning, incident coordination and auditable reporting. About NUBURU Subsidiary, Inc. NUBURU Subsidiary, Inc. wholly owns Lyocon S.r.l., an Italian laser technology company that designs, manufactures and integrates laser systems. Lyocon supports NUBURU’s industrial laser business and the development of photonics capabilities for potential dual-use applications. Forward-Looking Statements This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. These statements include plans for U.S. and allied market entry, pipeline conversion, procurement participation, demonstrations and technical evaluations, a potential U.S. presence and hangar, commercialization, partnerships and a potential expansion of the Maddox Defense collaboration. Future submissions and bids are subject to management approval and applicable competition and tender requirements. There is no assurance that Tekne or NUBURU will be selected, qualified or awarded any contract. The order, program and pipeline figures are preliminary, unaudited management measures previously disclosed on October 22, 2026 and presented at 100% of Tekne. The approximately $96.8 million remaining order and program value is based on the September operating schedule, includes conditional items and is not validated signed backlog. The approximately $259.8 million additional gross pipeline comprises 41 prospective opportunities that remain subject to procurement decisions and contract awards. These measures are not U.S. GAAP revenue or financial guidance. Realization depends on funding, production, delivery, customer acceptance and collection, and amounts and timing may change. USD values are approximate and use the previously disclosed reference exchange rate of $1.1551 per euro; actual U.S. GAAP translation rates may differ. Contract awards to third parties are market context only and are not indicative of results NUBURU may achieve. Actual results may differ materially due to selection and eligibility decisions, procurement timing and funding, technical qualification, partner negotiations, available resources, customer demand, Golden Power conditions, intellectual property, export and import controls, other required approvals, and the risks in NUBURU’s SEC filings. Statements speak as of this release’s date. NUBURU undertakes no obligation to update them except as required by law. articles.summary: New digital presence showcases the integrated Defense & Security platform and strengthens access to corporate and investor information DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- NUBURU, Inc. Tekne, Lyocon and Orbit, and the Company’s approach to technology integration and commercialization. Defense and civilian applications, the development roadmap, executive leadership and strategic advisers. articles.summary: Independent accountant’s interim review remains in process. The Company will provide a further update once the review is completed. DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- NUBURU, Inc. (NYSE American: BURU) today provided an update on its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, which the Company filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 23, 2026. At the time of filing, the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm had not completed its review of the interim financial statements included in that report. The review remains in process, including procedures relating to valuation and impairment matters. The financial statements and related disclosures in the Form 10-Q are therefore subject to completion of that review and may change. As of the date of this release, the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm has not informed the Company of any required adjustment to the financial statements included in the Form 10-Q. Until the review is completed, investors should consider the financial information in the Form 10-Q in light of the status of the review. NUBURU is working with its independent registered public accounting firm to complete the review as soon as possible. Once the review is completed, the Company will determine, together with its Audit Committee, securities counsel and independent registered public accounting firm, whether an amendment to the Form 10-Q or any other disclosure or filing is required. The Company will provide a further update, including a discussion of its third-quarter results, once the review is completed. About NUBURU, Inc. NUBURU, Inc. (NYSE American: BURU) develops systems for defense and security, critical infrastructure and digital resilience. Its Defense & Security platform combines photonics, electronic warfare, special vehicles, operational-resilience software and advanced manufacturing. Forward-Looking Statements This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. These statements include the completion, timing and outcome of the independent accountant’s interim review of the third-quarter financial statements, whether any amendment to the Form 10-Q or other disclosure or filing will be required, and the timing of future updates. Actual results may differ materially. Risks include the possibility that completion of the interim review results in changes to the financial statements or disclosures in the Form 10-Q, delays in completing the review, the consequences of the Form 10-Q having been filed before the review was completed, NUBURU’s need for additional financing and the substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern disclosed in its Form 10-Q. Other risks are described in NUBURU’s SEC filings. NUBURU undertakes no obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by law.
